'''Ju''' is a language from the [[West Chadic languages|West Chadian branch]] of the [[Chadic languages|Chadic language family]].<ref name="Blench, Roger">{{Cite web |last=Blench |first=Robert |author-link=Roger Blench |date=2006 |editor-last= |title=The Afro-Asiatic Languages. Classification and Reference List |url=http://rogerblench.info/Language/Afroasiatic/General/AALIST.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007050740/http://rogerblench.info/Language/Afroasiatic/General/AALIST.pdf |archive-date=2013-10-07 |website= |publisher=Roger Blench Website. Publications |pages=4–6 |language=en }}{{Retrieved|access-date=2016-11-30}}</ref><ref name="An Atlas of Nigerian Langages2">{{Cite web |last=Blench |first=Robert |author-link=Roger Blench |date=2012 |edition=3rd |title=An Atlas of Nigerian Languages |url=http://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/Nigeria/Atlas%20of%20Nigerian%20Languages-%20ed%20III.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130420192115/http://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/Nigeria/Atlas%20of%20Nigerian%20Languages-%20ed%20III.pdf  |archive-date=2013-04-20 |website=Roger Blench |language=en }}{{Retrieved|access-date=2016-11-30}}</ref> The language is spoken solely in [[Nigeria]], and had approximately 900 [[Native-speaker|native speakers]] in 1993. The language is unwritten.

== Classification ==
Ju is part of the Guruntum (Gurdung according to the work of [[Roger Blench]]) group of the [[South Bauchi languages|South Bauchi language group]], and is thus similar to the [[Guruntum language|Guruntum]], [[Tala language|Tala]], and [[Zangwal language|Zangwal]] languages.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Blench |first=Roger |date=2021-01-01 |title=West Chadic classification 2021 |website=Academia |url=https://www.academia.edu/58551549}}</ref>

== General Information ==
The Ju language is spoken primarily in the village of the same name, [[Ju, Nigeria|Ju]], which lies to the south of [[Bauchi (city)|Bauchi]]. The village is in the Bauchi [[Local government areas of Nigeria|local government area]] in the [[Bauchi State|state of Bauchi]].<ref name=":0" />

Ju shares [[language border]]s mostly with other [[West Chadic languages]]; Zangwal to the north, Tala to the northwest, the [[South Bauchi languages#Blench|Polchi language cluster]] to the west, and the [[Kir-Balar language]] to the south. To the east, Ju borders the [[sprachbund]] of the [[Dulbu language]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2016 |editor-last=Lewis |editor-first=M. Paul |editor2-last=Simons |editor2-first=Gary F. |editor3-last=Fennig |editor3-first=Charles D. |title=Nigeria, Map 3 |url=http://www.ethnologue.com/18/map/NG_03/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20161130181719/http://www.ethnologue.com/18/map/NG_03/ |archive-date=2016-11-30 |website=[[Ethnologue|Ethnologue: Languages of the World]] (19th Edition) |publisher=[[SIL International]] |pages= |language=en}}{{Retrieved|access-date=2016-11-30}}</ref>

Information on the number of speakers of the Ju language is varied: in 1971, Ju had around 150 speakers,<ref name="An Atlas of Nigerian Langages">{{Cite web |last=Blench |first=Robert |author-link=Roger Blench |date=2012 |edition=3rd |title=An Atlas of Nigerian Languages |url=http://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/Nigeria/Atlas%20of%20Nigerian%20Languages-%20ed%20III.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130420192115/http://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/Nigeria/Atlas%20of%20Nigerian%20Languages-%20ed%20III.pdf |archive-date=2013-04-20 |website=Roger Blench |page=45 |language=en }}{{Retrieved|access-date=2016-11-30}}</ref> and ''[[Ethnologue]]'' measured 900 in 1993. However, the [[Joshua Project]], has reported that Ju is used solely among the older generation, while the youth are switching to [[Hausa language|Hausa]].{{cn|date=March 2024}}
